fda: U.S. Food and Drug Administration: Halloween Food Safety Tips for Parents
aap: American Academy of Pediatrics (HealthyChildren.org): Halloween Safety Tips

tips.head: Eat first, check later
tips.body: Give children a meal or snack before they go, and have them wait to eat any treats until you have looked them over at home.

tips.head: Wrapped treats only
tips.body: Keep only commercially wrapped treats. Throw away anything unwrapped, torn, discoloured or with tiny pinholes.

tips.head: Be seen
tips.body: Choose bright costumes, add reflective tape or glow-in-the-dark details, and carry a flashlight after dark.

tips.head: Costumes that let them see and walk
tips.body: Prefer non-toxic face paint and hats to masks that block vision; keep costumes short enough not to trip on, and look for "flame resistant" on the label.

tips.head: Who goes with whom
tips.body: Always go with young children. Older children should go in a group, with a time to be back. No one goes into a home or a car for a treat.

tips.head: Crossing the street
tips.body: Stay on lit streets and sidewalks, cross together at crosswalks, and put phones and music away while walking and crossing.

tips.head: Food allergies
tips.body: Read labels; an allergic child should not eat home-baked treats, and should carry their prescribed emergency medicine.

tips.head: Teal pumpkins
tips.body: A teal pumpkin on a porch means that house has non-food treats, so children with food allergies can join in.

tips.head: The littlest ones
tips.body: For young children, take out choking hazards: gum, peanuts, hard sweets and small toys.
